marks.gloss_en: what is tia? Rav Yehuda: the root of a bitter herb
Rav Yehuda: one who eats three shekel[-weights] of asafoetida on an empty heart -- his skin sheds
Rav Yosef: one who eats sixteen eggs, forty nuts, seven caper-fruits and drinks a revi'it of honey in the Tammuz season, on an empty heart -- his heartstrings are uprooted
a young deer whose hind legs were cut: Rav examined it at the convergence of the sinews and declared it kosher
[Rav]: what is the remedy? [Shmuel]: let us set it in the oven -- it will examine itself
וכדרב חסדא -- as Rav Chisda: an animal found with cut hooves is inspected by its mouth
גמל ניבי אית ליה! -- a camel has cuspids, so the mouth inspection already excludes it (not answered: the proviso is emended to the young camel, p_chisda_makir_ben_gamal)
[the tooth sign is for] where its hooves were cut
דתני דבי רבי ישמעאל -- 'it': only the camel chews the cud and is non-kosher, so no other species defeats the mouth inspection
לאו אמרת איכא בן גמל? איכא נמי מינא אחרינא דדמי לבן גמל! -- perhaps another species resembles the young camel
לא סלקא דעתך -- the school of R' Yishmael: only the camel chews the cud and is non-kosher (= p_dvei_ri_hu_gamal)

the school of R' Yishmael: 'the camel, for it chews the cud' (Lev 11:4) -- the Ruler of His world knows there is nothing that chews the cud and is non-kosher but the camel; therefore the verse specified it with 'it'
וכללא הוא? והרי גמל -- it chews the cud, has no upper teeth, and is non-kosher!
גמל ניבי אית ליה -- a camel has cuspids (= p_gamal_nivei)
a camel has cuspids
והרי בן גמל -- a young camel has no cuspids either, and is non-kosher (not answered: the stam re-reads the baraita instead)
ותו, הרי שפן וארנבת -- they chew the cud and have upper teeth, and are non-kosher (not answered: the stam re-reads the baraita instead)
ועוד, שינים מי כתיבי באורייתא? -- teeth are not written in the Torah, yet the baraita lists them as the Torah's sign (not answered: the stam re-reads the baraita instead)
a young camel has no cuspids either
the baraita: any animal that chews the cud is known to have no upper teeth, and is kosher
דתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל -- 'it': only the pig parts the hoof and is non-kosher, so no other species defeats the hoof inspection
לאו אמרת איכא חזיר? איכא נמי מינא אחרינא דדמיא לחזיר! -- perhaps another species resembles the pig
לא סלקא דעתך -- the school of R' Yishmael: only the pig parts the hoof and is non-kosher (= p_dvei_ri_hu_chazir)

the school of R' Yishmael: 'the pig, for it parts the hoof' (Lev 11:7) -- the Ruler of His world knows there is nothing that parts the hoof and is non-kosher but the pig; therefore the verse specified it with 'it'
לאו אמרת איכא ערוד? איכא נמי מינא אחרינא דדמיא לערוד! -- perhaps another species resembles the arvad
גמירי דליכא -- it is learned by tradition that there is none
and where does he inspect [the flesh]? at the wings of the tailbone
Rav Chisda: one walking on the road who found an animal whose mouth was mutilated inspects its hooves: if they are cloven it is known to be kosher; if not, non-kosher

Rav Chisda: one walking in the wilderness who found an animal whose mouth was mutilated and whose hooves were cut inspects its flesh: if it runs warp and woof it is known to be kosher; if not, non-kosher
[the mishna's] 'the signs of an undomesticated animal' [were stated in the Torah]
the signs of a domesticated and an undomesticated animal were stated in the Torah
and of grasshoppers: any that has four legs, four wings, jumping legs, and whose wings cover most of it [is kosher]
